claims.text: Conventional single-phase ZrB2 requires processing temperatures above 2300 °C.
ZrB2 benefits from strong Zr–B and B–B bonding.
Lower-temperature-processed ZrB2 has insufficient oxidation resistance.
Lower-temperature-processed ZrB2 has insufficient resistance to liquid plating-metal corrosion.
Equiatomic Hf, Zr, Ta, Nb, and Ti cations can form a single-phase high-entropy diboride.
The proposed high-entropy diboride can be densified by spark plasma sintering at approximately 1700 °C.
High-energy ball milling can assist consolidation of the proposed high-entropy diboride.
The Hf–Zr–Ta–Nb–Ti high-entropy diboride can retain its shape during oxidation exposure at 1500 °C.
The proposed material is suitable for prolonged contact with liquid plating-metal baths.
The intervention produces a homogeneous single-phase diboride microstructure.
High-entropy alloying induces lattice distortion and refined grain boundaries in the proposed diboride.
Lattice distortion and refined grain boundaries promote densification at lower processing temperatures.
The high-entropy effect slows atomic diffusion.
The high-entropy effect enhances sintering kinetics at reduced temperatures.
Lattice distortion and a uniform microstructure promote robust protective oxide scales that inhibit oxygen ingress.
The proposed protective scales inhibit attack by liquid plating metals.
The high-entropy diboride will have lower oxidation weight gain than ZrB2 processed by the same fabrication route.
The high-entropy diboride will have comparable or improved densification and mechanical strength relative to conventional ZrB2.
The high-entropy diboride will exhibit lower liquid plating-metal corrosion rates than conventional ZrB2.

contradictions.description: The mechanism simultaneously invokes slowed atomic diffusion and enhanced low-temperature sintering kinetics without explaining how slower diffusion accelerates densification.

The predicted outcome permits merely comparable mechanical strength, whereas the falsification rule requires a statistically significant improvement greater than 20%; an outcome allowed by the prediction would therefore falsify the hypothesis.

The prediction includes improvement over prior lower-temperature specimens, but the experiment includes only high-entropy material processed near 1700 °C and conventional ZrB2 processed above 2300 °C, with no lower-temperature ZrB2 control.
